note: The EU's common visa list, Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 as consolidated on 30 December 2025, which binds every EU Member State but Ireland and, as a development of the Schengen acquis, Iceland, Norway, Switzerland and Liechtenstein: nationals of the countries in Annex I need a visa; those in Annex II (with Hong Kong and Macao SAR passports, British nationals who aren't British citizens such as the British Overseas Territories' citizens, Taiwan and Kosovo) may stay up to 90 days in any 180 without one (the footnotes' conditions, such as biometric passports for some, aren't modelled). EU citizens enter one another's territory with no visa or equivalent formality (Directive 2004/38, art. 5), and that right extends to Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway under the EEA Agreement and to Switzerland under its agreement on the free movement of persons. ETIAS, the travel authorisation Annex II's travellers will need, starts six months after the Entry/Exit System is fully in place, as the Commission says; it isn't modelled until it starts.

sources.title: Publications Office of the EU, Directive 2004/38/EC on the right of citizens of the Union and their family members to move and reside freely within the territory of the Member States, article 5
sources.said: Member States shall grant Union citizens leave to enter their territory with a valid identity card or passport and shall grant family members who are not nationals of a Member State leave to enter their territory with a valid passport. No entry visa or equivalent formality may be imposed on Union citizens.

sources.title: Publications Office of the EU, Decision of the EEA Joint Committee No 158/2007 amending Annex V and Annex VIII to the EEA Agreement
sources.said: Directive 2004/38/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 29 April 2004 on the right of citizens of the Union and their family members to move and reside freely within the territory of the Member States ... is to be incorporated into the Agreement.

sources.title: Publications Office of the EU, Agreement between the European Community and its Member States and the Swiss Confederation on the free movement of persons, Annex I, article 1
sources.said: shall allow nationals of the other Contracting Parties and members of their family within the meaning of Article 3 of this Annex and posted persons within the meaning of Article 17 of this Annex to enter their territory simply upon production of a valid identity card or passport. No entry visa or equivalent requirement may be demanded

sources.title: Publications Office of the EU, Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 (as adopted), recitals 35 to 37 and 39
sources.said: As regards Iceland and Norway, this Regulation constitutes a development of the provisions of the Schengen acquis ... As regards Switzerland, this Regulation constitutes a development of the provisions of the Schengen acquis ... As regards Liechtenstein, this Regulation constitutes a development of the provisions of the Schengen acquis ... Ireland is therefore not taking part in the adoption of this Regulation and is not bound by it or subject to its application

sources.title: European Commission, Migration and Home Affairs, Visa policy
sources.said: Visa-exempt travellers will need to fill out an online ETIAS form and pay a small fee before being able to travel to the Schengen Area, six months after the full implementation of Entry/Exit system (EES) .
